soundBank.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the SoundBank.

event.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the Event.

gameObject.description: The unique ID of the game object.

ak.soundengine.postEvent.description: Asynchronously post an Event to the sound engine (by event ID). See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::PostEvent</tt>.

return.description: The playing ID of the Event launched, or \c AK_INVALID_PLAYING_ID if posting the event failed.

ak.soundengine.postMsgMonitor.description: Display a message in the Profiler's Capture Log view.

gameObject.description: Associated game object ID. Its default value is the transport game object.

trigger.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the Trigger.

gameObject.description: ID of the game object to be registered. Valid range is [0, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFDF].

name.description: Name of the game object (for monitoring purpose).

ak.soundengine.registerGameObj.description: Register a game object. Registering a game object twice does nothing. Unregistering it once unregisters it no matter how many times it has been registered. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::RegisterGameObj</tt>.

gameObject.description: Associated game object ID. The default value is transport game object.

rtpc.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the real-time parameter control.

ak.soundengine.resetRTPCValue.description: Resets the value of a real-time parameter control to its default value, as specified in the Wwise project. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::ResetRTPCValue</tt>.

event.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the Event.

gameObject.description: Associated game object ID; use <tt>AK_INVALID_GAME_OBJECT</tt> to affect all game objects.

percent.description: Desired position where playback should restart, expressed in a percentage of the file's total duration, between 0 and 1.f. See note above about infinite looping sounds.

playingId.description: Specifies the playing ID for which the seek is to be applied. This results in the seek being applied only to active actions of the playing ID. Use \c AK_INVALID_PLAYING_ID or nothing, to seek on all active Actions of this Event ID.

position.description: Desired position where playback should restart, in milliseconds.

seekToNearestMarker.description: If true, the final seeking position is made equal to the nearest marker.

ak.soundengine.seekOnEvent.description: Seeks inside all playing objects that are referenced in Play Actions of the specified Event. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SeekOnEvent</tt>.

listeners.description: Array of listener game object IDs. Game objects must have been previously registered.

ak.soundengine.setDefaultListeners.description: Sets the default active listeners for all subsequent game objects that are registered. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetDefaultListeners</tt>.

auxBus.description: Either the ID (GUID), name or Short ID of the auxiliary bus.

controlValue.description: Value in the range [0.0f:1.0f], send level to auxiliary bus.

listener.description: Game object ID of the listener associated with this send.

ak.soundengine.setGameObjectAuxSendValue.description: Sets the Auxiliary Busses to route the specified game object. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetGameObjectAuxSendValues</tt>.

controlValue.description: A multiplier where 0 means silence and 1 means no change. Therefore, values between 0 and 1 attenuate the sound, and values greater than 1 amplify it.

ak.soundengine.setGameObjectOutputBusVol.description: Set the output bus volume (direct) to be used for the specified game object. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetGameObjectOutputBusVolume</tt>.

channelConfig.description: Channel configuration associated with volumeOffsets. Use <tt>AK::AkChannelConfig::Serialize</tt> to serialize the value.

spatialized.description: Spatialization toggle (true: enable spatialization, false: disable spatialization).

volumeOffsets.description: Array of per-speaker volume offsets, in dB. See AkSpeakerVolumes.h for how to manipulate this array.

ak.soundengine.setListenerSpatialization.description: Sets a listener's spatialization parameters. This lets you define listener-specific volume offsets for each audio channel. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetListenerSpatialization</tt>.

listeners.description: Array of listener game object IDs. Game objects must have been previously registered.

ak.soundengine.setListeners.description: Sets a single game object's active listeners. By default, all new game objects have no listeners active, but this behavior can be overridden with <tt>SetDefaultListeners()</tt>. Inactive listeners are not computed. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetListeners</tt>.

position.description: A 3D position to set for the game object.

ak.soundengine.setMultiplePositions.description: Sets multiple positions for a single game object. Setting multiple positions for a single game object is a way to simulate multiple emission sources while using the resources of only one voice. This can be used to simulate wall openings, area sounds, or multiple objects emitting the same sound in the same area. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetMultiplePositions</tt>.

ak.soundengine.setObjectObstructionAndOc.description: Set a game object's obstruction and occlusion levels. This function is used to affect how an object should be heard by a specific listener. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetObjectObstructionAndOcclusion</tt>.

position.description: The 3D position to set for the game object.

ak.soundengine.setPosition.description: Sets the position of a game object. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetPosition</tt>.

gameObject.description: Associated game object ID. The default value is transport game object.

rtpc.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the real-time parameter control.

ak.soundengine.setRTPCValue.description: Sets the value of a real-time parameter control. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetRTPCValue</tt>.

attenuationScalingFactor.description: The scaling factor, where 1 means 100%, 0.5 means 50%, 2 means 200%, and so on.

ak.soundengine.setScalingFactor.description: Sets the scaling factor of a game object. You can modify the attenuation computations on this game object to simulate sounds with a larger or smaller affected areas. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetScalingFactor</tt>.

state.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the State.

stateGroup.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the State Group.

ak.soundengine.setState.description: Sets the State of a State Group. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetState</tt>.

gameObject.description: Associated game object ID. Its default value is the transport game object.

switchGroup.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or short ID of the Switch Group.

switchState.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the Switch State.

ak.soundengine.setSwitch.description: Sets the State of a Switch Group. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::SetSwitch</tt>.

gameObject.description: Specify a game object to stop only playback associated to the provided game object ID.

ak.soundengine.stopAll.description: Stop playing the current content associated to the specified game object ID. If no game object is specified, all sounds are stopped. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::StopAll</tt>.

fadeCurve.description: Curve type to be used for the transition. Uses values from \ref AkCurveInterpolation .

ak.soundengine.stopPlayingID.description: Stops the current content, associated to the specified playing ID, from playing. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::StopPlayingID</tt>.

soundBank.description: Either the ID (GUID), name, or Short ID of the SoundBank.

gameObject.description: ID of the game object to be unregistered. Valid range is [0, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFDF]. Use \c AK_INVALID_GAME_OBJECT to unregister all game objects.

ak.soundengine.unregisterGameObj.description: Unregisters a game object. Registering a game object twice does nothing. Unregistering it once unregisters it no matter how many times it has been registered. Unregistering a game object while it is in use is allowed, but the control over the parameters of this game object is lost. For example, say a sound associated with this game object is a 3D moving sound. It stops moving when the game object is unregistered, and there is no way to regain control over the game object. See <tt>AK::SoundEngine::UnregisterGameObj</tt>.

copy-from-platform.description: The platform to copy settings from.

new-platform-name.description: The name of the new platform.

ak.wwise.cli.addNewPlatform.description: Adds a new platform to a project. The platform must not already exist.

output.description: Allows you to follow this option with a platform, and a path to an output directory to override the output directory of this platform. Repeat this option for other platforms. If only an output directory is specified, sources for all platforms are generated in that directory.

platform.description: Specifies for which platforms the sources are converted using the project settings. This option must be followed by the platform identifiers.

source-by-platform.description: Specifies the WSOURCES files to use by platform. When specified for a specific platform, it overrides the WSOURCES files from the project settings for this platform. For platforms for which this is not specified, the project settings are used. Specify the platform first, then the WSOURCES files to use for this platform. Repeat the operation for each platform and WSOURCES file.

source-file.description: Specifies the WSOURCES files to use. Those WSOURCES files are used for all platforms.

ak.wwise.cli.convertExternalSource.description: External sources conversion. Converts the external sources files for the specified project. Optionally, additional WSOURCES can be specified. External Sources are a special type of source that you can put in a sound object in Wwise. It indicates that the real sound data will be provided at runtime. While external source conversion can be triggered by SoundBank generation, this operation can be used to process sources not contained in the Wwise Project. Refer to \ref integrating_external_sources.

platform.description: Specifies which platform the new project supports. If not specified, Windows only is used.

ak.wwise.cli.createNewProject.description: Creates a blank new project. The project must not already exist. If the directory does not exist, it is created.

content.description: Content to output from the object model. Default is 'name'.

no-session.description: Specify to skip objects with session lifetime.

output.description: Full path of the output file

ak.wwise.cli.dumpObjects.description: Dump the objects model of a project as a JSON file.

do-file.description: Specify an array of Lua files to load before the main Lua script is loaded and executed. This option must be followed by a absolute file name.

lua-path.description: Specify a search path for Lua modules loaded. This option must be followed by a Lua path. Ex: '--lua-path C:\\module\\?.lua'

lua-script.description: Specify the file path of the main Lua script to load and execute.

project.description: When no project is specified, no project is loaded. Refer to \ref ak_wwise_console_project_open for information on how to open a project.

require.description: Specify an array of Lua module to load at runtime using the require system. This option must be followed by a Lua module name. The module name must be found in the Lua path. Ex: '--require debug.lua'

watchdog-timeout.description: Time in seconds to set as a watchdog threshold. The watchdog is signaled every time a WAAPI function call is made. By default, the value is 0 and the watchdog is disabled.

ak.wwise.cli.executeLuaScript.description: Execute a Lua script. Optionally, specify additional Lua search paths, additional modules, and additional Lua scripts to load prior to the main script. The script can return a value. All arguments will be passed to the Lua script in the "wa_args" global variable.

result.description: Result returned by the Lua script

bank.description: Specifies which SoundBanks are generated. This option must be followed by the name of the SoundBank to be generated. Multiple SoundBanks can be specified. If no SoundBank is specified, all SoundBanks are generated. Alternatively, a text file containing a list of SoundBank names can be specified, by specifying the full path to the text file, including the extension '.txt'.

cache.description: Overrides the project's cache directory path and instead uses the (relative) path specified in the command.

clear-audio-file-cache.description: Deletes the content of the Wwise audio file cache directory prior to converting source files and generating SoundBanks, which ensures that all source files are reconverted. Note that the whole cache is cleared, for all platforms, regardless of the --platform option.

custom-post-gen-cmd.description: Overrides the custom post-generation step command line that was defined for this platform in Wwise. This option must be followed by the platform identifier (listed above), followed again by the new command line (use quotes if there are spaces). To override the custom post-generation step command line of another platform, repeat the option --custom-post-gen-cmd followed by the other platform's identifier and its new command line. An empty string ("") specified for the command-line means no post-generation step is executed.

custom-pre-gen-cmd.description: Overrides the custom pre-generation step command line that was defined for this platform in Wwise. This option must be followed by the platform identifier (listed above), followed again by the new command line (use quotes if there are spaces). To override the custom pre-generation step command line of another platform, repeat the option --custom-pre-gen-cmd followed by the other platform's identifier and its new command line. An empty string ("") specified for the command-line means no pre-generation step is executed.

header-file.description: Generates the header file Wwise_IDs.h, even if this option is not specified in the project settings.

header-file-path.description: (DEPRECATED) Use root-output-path instead. Overrides the header file path specified in the project settings. This option must be followed by the path (absolute or relative) in which the header file (Wwise_IDs.h) will be written. This is only effective if the header file's creation is required.

import-definition-file.description: Imports a SoundBank definition file. This option must be followed by the full path of the bank definition file to be imported. Multiple files can be specified. If the option --save is not specified, the changes made to the project as a result of the imported definition file do not persist.

language.description: Specifies the languages for which the SoundBanks are generated. This option must be followed by a language identifier defined in the project. Each specified language must be prefixed with this option.

license.description: Sets the license to be used. The license is not saved in the project.

license-file.description: Sets the license to the contents of the file specified. The license is not saved in the project.

no-decode.description: Avoids generating DECODED files in the .cache directory, which saves CPU and disk space for your Wwise project. It also reduces the SoundBank generation time. Warning: If you do not generate the DECODED files, playing back these sounds in Wwise Authoring could result in an outdated playback or no playback at all. Clearing the file cache is recommended after using this option.

no-source-control.description: Skip the Source Control operations, even it is was enabled in the SoundBank Project Settings.

output.description: Allows you to follow this option with a platform and an output path to override the output path of this platform for external source conversion. Repeat this option for other platforms. If only a directory is specified, sources for all platforms are generated in that directory.

platform.description: Specifies the platforms for which SoundBanks are generated. This option must be followed by the platform identifiers.

readable-soundbanks.description: Generates readable SoundBanks (.rbnk), even if this option is not specified in the project settings.

root-output-path.description: Overrides the root output path specified in the SoundBank settings. This option must be followed by the path (absolute or relative) in which the project level, platform agnostic files will be written. Examples of such files are Wwise_IDs.h and ProjectInfo.(xml|json).

save.description: Saves the project before generating SoundBanks. If a tab-delimited import file was provided, the imported content is saved as well. Saving also migrates the project first, if required. This option does not save the project for other instances of Wwise that are currently running.

skip-languages.description: Will not generate any localized SoundBank in the project.

soundbank-path.description: Overrides the SoundBank path specified for this platform. This option must be followed by the platform identifier (listed above), followed again by the new path (absolute or relative, use quotes if there are spaces). To override the path of another platform, repeat the option --soundbank-path followed by the other platform's specifier and its new path.

source-by-platform.description: Specifies the WSOURCES files to use by platform for external source conversion. When specified for a specific platform, it overrides the WSOURCES files from the project settings for this platform. For platforms for which this is not specified, the project settings are used. Specify the platform first, then the WSOURCES files to use for this platform. Repeat the operation for each platform and WSOURCES file.

source-file.description: Specifies the WSOURCES files to use for external source conversion. Those WSOURCES files are used for all platforms.

tab-delimited-import-file.description: The tab delimited file to import. Multiple files to import can be specified after this option.

use-stable-guid.description: Give the SoundBank a stable GUID across multiple builds if you don't want to save the project.

use-user-overrides.description: Use user overrides for Project Settings and SoundBank Settings.

ak.wwise.cli.generateSoundbank.description: SoundBank generation. SoundBank generation is performed according to the settings stored in the project. User SoundBanks Settings are normally ignored when SoundBank generation is launched from the command line. However, when using the Source Control for generated SoundBanks, the User Project Settings are loaded for the Source Control settings. Also, some of these settings can be overridden from the command line.

result.description: The process exit code of SoundBank generation. Although your SoundBanks might generate properly with warnings, it is strongly recommended that you consider these warnings as errors. For example, WwiseConsole.exe returns an error code when a source file is missing. Although a missing source file does not prevent your SoundBanks from being generated, the resulting SoundBanks might potentially be incomplete. You can change the severity of most messages encountered during the SoundBank Generation by going to Project Settings > Logs, in Wwise. Changing the severity of the messages impacts the return codes.

ak.wwise.cli.moveMediaIdsToSingleFile.description: Moves the project's media IDs from its work units (.wwu) to a single file, <project-name>.mediaid.  This command forces a save of all the project's work units.

ak.wwise.cli.moveMediaIdsToWorkUnits.description: Moves the project's media IDs from a single xml file <project-name>.mediaid to its work units (.wwu).  This command forces a save of all the project's work units.

no-source-control.description: Skip automatic addition and checkout (if supported by project's source control plugin) of new and modified files to source control.

tab-delimited-import-file.description: The tab delimited file to import.

ak.wwise.cli.tabDelimitedImport.description: Imports a tab-delimited file to create and modify different object hierarchies. The project is automatically migrated (if required). It is also automatically saved following the import.

ak.wwise.cli.updateMediaIdsInSingleFile.description: Loads the project and updates the contents of <project-name>.mediaid, if it exists.

ak.wwise.cli.verify.description: Loads the project and does nothing else. This is useful to see the log for verification purposes without actually migrating and saving.

allowed-addr.description: Specifies the IP addresses that are allowed to connect to WAAPI. This option must be followed by a comma-separated list, for example: "127.0.0.1". Default value is "127.0.0.1".

allowed-origin.description: Specifies the hosts that are allowed to connect to WAAPI. This option must be followed by a comma-separated list, for example: "www.myhost.com,www.myhost2.com". Validation is performed on the HTTP header Origin. Connections that do not provide the Origin header, as well as file-based connections (for example: file://), are always allowed.

http-max-clients.description: Specifies the maximum number of concurrent WAAPI clients that can connect to the server when using HTTP POST. This option must be followed by a number between 0 and 100. Using 0 prevents the server from running. Default value is 2.

http-port.description: Specifies the port number used by WAAPI when using HTTP POST. This option must be followed by a port number between 0 and 65,535. Using 0 prevents the server from running. Default value is 8090.

project.description: When no project is specified, no project is loaded. Refer to \ref ak_wwise_console_project_open for information on how to open a project.

wamp-max-clients.description: Specifies the maximum number of concurrent WAAPI clients that can connect to the server when using WAMP. This option must be followed by a number between 0 and 100. Using 0 prevents the server from running. Default value is 5.

wamp-port.description: Specifies the port number used by WAAPI when using WAMP. This option, which takes precedence over the User Preferences, must be followed by a port number between 0 and 65,535. Using 0 prevents the server from running. Default value is 8080.

watchdog-timeout.description: Time in seconds to set as a watchdog threshold. The watchdog is signaled every time a WAAPI function call is made. By default, the value is 0 and the watchdog is disabled.

ak.wwise.cli.waapiServer.description: Starts a command-line Wwise Authoring API server, to which client applications, using the Wwise Authoring API, can connect.

ak.wwise.console.project.close.description: Closes the current project. This operation is synchronous.

hadProjectOpen.description: True if there was a project open, false otherwise. Note that if there was no project open, no ak.wwise.core.project.preClosed or ak.wwise.core.project.postClosed event is issued.

languages.description: Array of languages to creates for this project. If not specified, the English(US) language is created. When multiple languages are specified, the first one becomes the default language.

path.description: The path to the project WPROJ file. The path must use the same name for the WPROJ and the parent directory folder. For example: c:\\Projects\\MYPROJECT\\MYPROJECT.wproj. For using WAAPI on Mac, please refer to \ref waapi_path_on_mac .

platforms.description: Specifies the platform or platforms supported by the new project. If not specified, only Windows is used.

ak.wwise.console.project.create.description: Creates, saves and opens new empty project, specified by path and platform. The project has no factory setting WorkUnit. This operation is synchronous.

autoCheckOutToSourceControl.description: Determines if Wwise automatically performs a Checkout source control operation for affected work units and for the project. Defaults to true.

onMigrationRequired.description: The action to be executed when opening a project that needs to be migrated.

path.description: The path to the project WPROJ file. For using WAAPI on Mac, please refer to \ref waapi_path_on_mac .

ak.wwise.console.project.open.description: Opens a project, specified by path. This operation is synchronous.

languages.description: An array of languages. Each language is a unique name.

items.description: A language is a unique name.

objects.description: An array of objects. Each object is an ID (GUID), name, or object path.

platforms.description: An array of platforms. Each platform is an ID (GUID) or a unique name.

ak.wwise.core.audio.convert.description: Creates a converted audio file. When errors occur, this function returns a list of messages with corresponding levels of severity.

errors.description: List of logged entries with associated messages and severities.

items.description: Logged entry with severity and message.

message.description: Message logged by the system (Error or warning).

autoAddToSourceControl.description: Determines if Wwise automatically performs a source control Add operation on the imported files. Defaults to true.

autoCheckOutToSourceControl.description: Determines if Wwise automatically performs a source control Checkout operation (when applicable) on the modified files. Defaults to true.

default.description: Default values for each item in "imports". Use this object to avoid repeating common properties of every imported element.

^@[:_a-zA-Z0-9]+$.description: Specifies a Wwise object property and its value. Property names are prefixed with @. Refer to \ref wobjects_index for the properties available. For example: \@Volume:3

audioFile.description: Path to media file to import. This path must be accessible from Wwise. For using WAAPI on Mac, please refer to \ref waapi_path_on_mac .

audioFileBase64.description: Base64 encoded WAV audio file data to import with its target file path relative to the Originals folder, separated by a vertical bar. E.g. 'MySound.wav|UklGRu...'.

audioSourceNotes.description: The "Notes" field of the created audio source object.

dialogueEvent.description: Defines the path and name of a Dialogue Event to be created for the imported object. Refer to Tab Delimited Import in the Wwise Help documentation for more information.

event.description: Defines the path and name of an Event to be created for the imported object. Refer to Tab Delimited Import in the Wwise Help documentation for more information.

importLanguage.description: Imports the language for the audio file import (taken from the project's defined languages, found in the WPROJ file LanguageList).

importLocation.description: Object ID (GUID), name, or path used as root relative object paths.

notes.description: The "Notes" field of the created object.

objectPath.description: The path and name of the object(s) to be created. The path uses backslashes and can either be absolute or relative. Object types can be specified before the name. For example: \verbatim \\Actor-Mixer Hierarchy\\Default Work Unit\\<Random Container>MyContainer\\<Sound>MySound. \endverbatim Refer to \ref wobjects_index for the available types.

objectType.description: Specifies the type of object to create when importing an audio file. This type can also be specified directly in the objectPath. Refer to \ref wobjects_index for the available types.

originalsSubFolder.description: Specifies the 'originals' sub-folder in which to place the imported audio file. This folder is relative to the 'originals' folder in which the file would normally be imported. Example: if importing an SFX, then the audio file is imported to the folder Originals\\SFX\\originalsPath.

switchAssignation.description: Defines a Switch Group or State Group that is associated to a Switch Container, within the Actor-Mixer Hierarchy only. Also defines which Switch Container's child is assigned to which Switch or State from the associated group. Refer to Tab Delimited Import in the Wwise Help documentation for more information.

items.description: Import command. The members of this object are combined with those of "default", with this object's members having precedence. In addition to the listed properties, you can also set wobject properties and references using \@Property. For example, you can set the volume by adding the \@Volume property. References that have constraints from other references, such as a Switch Container's State/Switch, which is constrained to being a child of a State/Switch Group, should not be set because WAAPI cannot ensure that a reference is set in the required order.

^@[:_a-zA-Z0-9]+$.description: Specifies the value of the property. Refer to \ref wobjects_index for the properties available.

importLocation.description: Object ID (GUID), name, or path used as root relative object paths.

ak.wwise.core.audio.import.description: Creates Wwise objects and imports audio files. This function does not return an error when something fails during the import process, please refer to the log for the result of each import command. This function uses the same importation processor available through the Tab Delimited import in the Audio File Importer. The function returns an array of all objects created, replaced or re-used. Use the options to specify how the objects are returned. For more information, refer to \ref waapi_import.

optionsSchema.description: Specifies the return options for every object returned.

files.description: The list of imported original files.

items.description: Absolute path to the original file.
A log entry for audio import.

index.description: The index of the import command to which the log applies.

message.description: The description message of the log item.

In addition to the listed properties, you can also set wobject properties and references using \@Property. For example, you can set the volume by adding the \@Volume property. References that have constraints from other references, such as a Switch Container's State/Switch, which is constrained to being a child of a State/Switch Group, should not be set because WAAPI  cannot ensure that a reference is set in the required order.

autoAddToSourceControl.description: Determines if Wwise automatically performs a source control Add operation on the imported files. Defaults to true.

autoCheckOutToSourceControl.description: Determines if Wwise automatically performs a source control Checkout operation (when applicable) on the modified files. Defaults to true.

importFile.description: Location of tab-delimited import file. For using WAAPI on Mac, please refer to \ref waapi_path_on_mac .

importLanguage.description: Imports language for audio file import (taken from the project's defined languages, found in the WPROJ file LanguageList).

importLocation.description: Object ID (GUID), name, or path used as root relative object paths.

importOperation.description:
Determines how import object creation is performed. For each object created:
- createNew: creates a new object; the object is given the desired name if possible, otherwise a new unique name is used.
- useExisting: uses the object if it exists, updating the specified properties; otherwise it creates a new object. This is the default value.
- replaceExisting: creates a new object. If an existing object has the same name, the existing object is destroyed.

ak.wwise.core.audio.importTabDelimited.description: Scripted object creation and audio file import from a tab-delimited file.

optionsSchema.description: Specifies the return options for every object returned.

items.description: Objects that have been imported in the process of the tab delimited import. The objects have the properties specified in the return option, if applicable.

ak.wwise.core.audio.imported.description: Sent at the end of an import operation.

return.description: Data to be returned for every imported object.

files.description: The list of imported original files.

items.description: Absolute path to the original file.

objects.description: The list of objects that have been created as part of the same import operation.

items.description: Object created during the import operation. Default return is id and name.

operation.description: The operation applied for this import call.

objects.description: An array of objects to mute.

value.description: Whether the object is muted or not.

conversion.description: The object used for conversion. An object is an ID (GUID).

platform.description: The platform to which the settings apply. A platform is an ID (GUID) or a unique name.

plugin.description: Name of the plug-in to use for future conversions

ak.wwise.core.audio.setConversionPlugin.description: Changes the plug-in to use for audio file conversion.

objects.description: An array of objects to solo.

items.description: The ID (GUID), name, or path of the object to solo.

value.description: Whether the object is soloed or not.

getCrossChannelPeaks.description: When true, peaks are calculated globally across channels, instead of per channel.

numPeaks.description: The number of peaks that are required (minimum 1).

object.description: The ID (GUID), name, or path of the audio source object.

timeFrom.description: The start time, in seconds, of the section of the audio source for which peaks are required. This number must be smaller than timeTo.
